Q27865796.summary: Beneath a round arch at the centre of this golden book-box, Christ hangs on the cross in repoussé relief, with the Virgin and John below and the sun and moon above; a chalice stands at the foot of the cross. Enamelled symbols of the four evangelists fill the corners of a frame studded with pearls and gems. The inscriptions beneath the cross record Christ's words from the cross to his mother and to the beloved disciple.
facts: The Louvre records the inscriptions ECCE MATER TUA and ECCE FILIUS TUUS ('Behold your mother', 'Behold your son') beside the figures under the cross.
Another inscription states that a woman named Beatrix had the work made; her identity is uncertain.
The Louvre identifies it with the book-box from the treasury of Saint Servatius, Maastricht, which in 1677 held the text on which the Dukes of Brabant swore their oath; it was seized in 1795.

Q28065719.summary: This corner fragment of a sarcophagus front shows a veiled woman seated solemnly on a high-backed chair, holding a swaddled infant on her lap; a bearded man with a scroll leans on the chair behind her, another man appears at the corner, and two women stand at the right, one of whom seems to touch the child. It is one of the earliest sculpted images of the Virgin and Child, probably part of an Adoration of the Magi or a scene of the Nativity.
facts: The fragment was acquired by the Musée Saint-Raymond in 1986 from a private collection near Uzès (Gard).

Scholars have suggested that the woman touching the child is the midwife Salome of the apocryphal Protoevangelium of James, and that the missing right part may have shown the Magi or the first bath of the newborn.
It measures about 55 × 50 cm and comes from a continuous-frieze sarcophagus.
Q28065719.notes: Dating: POP gives 300–350, the Sathma corpus 325–350. The exact narrative scene is uncertain. Wikidata records 400.
Q28065719.original_title: Cuve de sarcophage de la Vierge à l'Enfant

cur:catacombs-generosa-christ-martyrs.summary: A detached, badly damaged fresco shows a row of five nimbed figures standing frontally against a light ground; the figure at the centre is Christ, flanked by four nimbed saints, probably the local martyrs. The painting – known as the 'crowning of the martyrs' – shows Christ welcoming and rewarding the saints whose tomb drew pilgrims to this small catacomb.
facts: The fresco is displayed as a detached panel, mounted in a frame, as the photograph shows.
cur:catacombs-generosa-christ-martyrs.notes: Commons supplies no description beyond the title 'coronatio martyrum'; the date and the names of the flanking saints are given here only in general terms. The image is small (460 px).
